model_context.note: Hero-model predictions not present on disk. qwen3_finetuned used as proxy -- both achieve ~random-guess performance on lesion_motion_direction (5-class, 20% baseline). Frames and question IDs are identical.

wrong_example.question: In which direction does the lesion drift over the frames?

right_example.question: In which direction does the lesion drift over the frames?

qa_notes.consecutive_clips: Wrong example ends at frame 28553; right example starts at 28560. Same post-resection lesion site.
qa_notes.mode_collapse: Model only ever predicts 'downward' or 'upward' -- never 'left', 'right', or 'stable'. Output distribution: downward=38/50 (76%), upward=12/50 (24%). Confusion: GT=stable: 5 downward + 5 upward (0% correct); GT=left/right: 16 downward + 4 upward (0% correct); GT=upward: 2 upward (20% correct); GT=downward: 9 downward (90% correct). Overall 22/50 = 22% correct -- barely above 20% random-guess baseline.
qa_notes.why_hard: Each clip = 1.12s. Motion is subtle. No cross-frame temporal attention -- model sees 8 independent frames.
qa_notes.dataset: All 50 lesion_motion_direction test samples from video 002-004 (83M, Olympus, 25fps, BBPS=9, 3 lesions, 21-min procedure).
qa_notes.insight_for_slide: These two clips are CONSECUTIVE (wrong ends at #28553, right starts at #28560). The model gives the SAME answer ('downward') for both. When GT happens to be 'downward', it looks correct. This is not temporal reasoning -- it is mode collapse on a learned prior.
